description: Fix supervisor false-terminal after a correct story + sidecar never dispatching review when all stories pass: align readWorkerOutcome with worker-report.json (push-model), tolerate string lastCompletedStory, gate hasPendingStories on review verdict, guard against stale reports, emit fallback events, and prove the fix end-to-end via a regression test plus an operator dogfood.
relatedDocs: FLOW.md (§4 cam next/sidecar, §7 autonomous loop / state-primary CAM-32, §8 state machine, §9 Q1 worker-report.json primary gate)

userStories.title: readWorkerOutcome falls back to worker-report.json and tolerates string lastCompletedStory
userStories.description: As the supervisor, I need readWorkerOutcome to derive the completed story from worker-report.json when handoff.json has no usable lastCompletedStory.id AND the captured pane text has no DONE sentinel, and to tolerate a malformed handoff where lastCompletedStory is a bare string instead of {id,title}, so a correctly-implemented story is never degraded to 'unknown' (terminal-blocked) just because the pane scrollback was idle by the time the supervisor captured it.
acceptanceCriteria: ReadWorkerOutcomeOptions gains an optional workerReportPath field (absolute path) wired through src/supervisor/loop.ts (the fileReader adapter) and src/supervisor/host.ts (buildSupervisorOptions, alongside prdPath/handoffPath). [oracle: grep -q "workerReportPath" src/supervisor/result.ts src/supervisor/loop.ts src/supervisor/host.ts]

When handoff.lastCompletedStory is a STRING (e.g. "US-001"), readWorkerOutcome coerces it to {id: "<the string>"} and resolves the outcome as before (pass/incomplete via the existing prd.passes:true check). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/result.test.ts]

When neither handoff.lastCompletedStory.id nor a DONE sentinel yields a story id, but worker-report.json exists with outcome=DONE and story=<id>, the function uses that story id and runs the existing prd passes:true verification (returns 'pass' or 'incomplete' accordingly). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/result.test.ts]

When worker-report.json has outcome starting with BLOCKED_, the outcome is 'blocked' with the report's story id and the BLOCKED_ token in detail (same shape as the sentinel-BLOCKED branch). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/result.test.ts]
When no worker-report.json exists, no handoff id, and no DONE sentinel, the outcome stays 'unknown' (byte-for-byte unchanged with the existing test). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/result.test.ts]

The detail string names which signal won: 'handoff-string-coerced', 'worker-report-fallback', or the existing 'handoff matches' / 'no sentinel, state-primary' wording. [oracle: grep -q "worker-report-fallback\|handoff-string-coerced" src/supervisor/result.ts]
Typecheck passes. [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass. [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Touch src/supervisor/result.ts (extend ReadWorkerOutcomeOptions; add a readWorkerReport branch under the existing 'Step 4: State-primary outcome' block at result.ts:256-294; tolerate string handoff in readHandoff around lines 130-139 or by coercing inside readWorkerOutcome). acceptanceCriteria: makeHasPendingStories is exported from src/commands/sidecar.ts so unit tests can import it directly (today it is module-private). [oracle: grep -q "^export function makeHasPendingStories" src/commands/sidecar.ts]
makeHasPendingStories returns true when at least one non-operator story has passes !== true (existing behavior preserved). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-loop.test.ts]

makeHasPendingStories returns false when all non-operator stories pass AND prd.review.lastVerdict is 'MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT'. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-loop.test.ts]

The terminal-verdict set used here matches the one in src/supervisor/decide.ts (TERMINAL_VERDICTS = ['CLEAN', 'MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT']) — either by import or by a co-located constant with a comment pointing to decide.ts. [oracle: grep -q "CLEAN\|MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT" src/commands/sidecar.ts]

userStories.title: Staleness guard: worker-report fallback only trusts a report whose story matches the expected dispatched story
userStories.description: As the supervisor, I need the worker-report.json fallback (US-001) to refuse a STALE report from a previous story — otherwise a leftover report on disk would flip a false-terminal into a worse false-pass, defeating the fix. The supervisor knows the advisory/just-dispatched story id (loop.ts `advisoryStoryId`); the fallback must compare report.story against it and ignore mismatches.
acceptanceCriteria: ReadWorkerOutcomeOptions gains an optional `expectedStoryId` field carrying the dispatched story id; loop.ts (around 770-775) passes `advisoryStoryId` into the call. [oracle: grep -q "expectedStoryId" src/supervisor/result.ts src/supervisor/loop.ts]

When worker-report.json exists with outcome=DONE and story matches expectedStoryId, the fallback path is taken (verifies prd.passes:true; returns pass/incomplete). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/result.test.ts]

When worker-report.json exists with outcome=DONE but story does NOT match expectedStoryId (stale report), the fallback is REJECTED and readWorkerOutcome behaves as if the report were absent (returns 'unknown' when no other signals exist). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/result.test.ts]

When expectedStoryId is undefined (older callers or tests not threading it), the fallback degrades gracefully: it uses the report as in US-001 (no regression vs US-001 behavior). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/result.test.ts]

When expectedStoryId is provided, a stale BLOCKED_* report whose story does NOT match expectedStoryId is rejected (does not produce a kind:blocked outcome for the dispatched story). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/result.test.ts]
Typecheck passes. [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass. [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Touch src/supervisor/result.ts (extend ReadWorkerOutcomeOptions and the US-001 fallback branch), src/supervisor/loop.ts:758-775 (thread advisoryStoryId from loop.ts:594 into readWorkerOutcome opts). src/supervisor/host.ts is unaffected (the field is set per-call by loop.ts, not built by host.ts). Note clearWorkerReport (loop.ts:625, host.ts:87-98) already wipes the file before dispatch, so the freshness guard here is the second line of defense against a clearWorkerReport failure or a worker that writes a report then crashes. Tests in test/supervisor/result.test.ts. Re-check FLOW.md §9-Q1 for the push-model assumption.

userStories.title: Operator dogfood: full cam run loop completes a multi-story PRD without manual re-arm and auto-dispatches review
userStories.description: As the operator, I run a real `cam run` + `cam next` dogfood against a multi-story PRD on this branch and confirm: (a) the loop flows story → story → … → review with NO manual per-story re-arm; (b) when the last non-operator story passes, the sidecar dispatches the review automatically; (c) no false-terminal 'blocked' notification fires after a correct story. Unit tests pass with green CI today on broken code (CAM-55 lesson), so the live ceremony is the real proof.
acceptanceCriteria: Operator runs `bun run build:release && bun run install:user` (or equivalent reinstall ceremony for the dogfood machine) so `cam` on PATH is the branch binary. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

Operator starts a fresh `cam run` session in a multi-story PRD repo and issues `cam next`; the supervisor implements at least two stories back-to-back with NO manual re-arm of the active flag between them. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

After the last non-operator story passes, the sidecar enters the supervisor and dispatches the review worker WITHOUT operator intervention (visible in the worker pane and in `.claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl`). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

No 'blocked' terminal notification fires between correctly-completed stories (no `notifyTerminal('blocked')` call in cam-worker-events.jsonl after a story that has passes:true in prd.json and a successful push). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Operator reports the ceremony outcome in the PR/issue thread (pass or specific failure mode) — this is the launch-ready evidence the PR needs. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The CAM-56 dogfood that surfaced the bug is the inverse ceremony: a successful repeat of that flow on this branch is the proof.
